text:
The Rangers scored three goals in the first 13:53 in Seattle, chased Joey Daccord, and then spent the third period finding out how much of that cushion they would need. Nearly all of it. Joonas Korpisalo stopped Jordan Eberle with 24 seconds left, the save our win probability model rated the biggest of the night, and New York held on 4-3 for its third straight win.

The first period was as lopsided as the score. The Rangers out-chanced Seattle 2.39 to 0.93 in expected goals (the quality of chances). Gabe Perreault scored 1:35 in off a Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafrenière setup, and Tye Kartye tipped in a power-play goal at 9:05 against the team that lost him on waivers. Jaroslav Chmelar made it 3-0 on a 42 percent chance, and Daccord, who had allowed three on 10 shots, gave way to Philipp Grubauer. Grubauer was good, 15 saves on 16, but Pavel Dorofeyev beat him on a backhand in the second for 4-0, again set up by Zibanejad and Lafrenière.

Then the Kraken pushed. Kaapo Kakko, the former Ranger, scored 1:50 into the third, Eberle added a power-play goal at 6:38, and Vince Dunn's slap shot at 15:02, a 5 percent chance, made it 4-3 and lifted Seattle from 2 percent to 13. Seattle out-chanced New York 1.52 to 1.11 in the period and put real pressure on Korpisalo, who stopped 25 of 28.

Over the whole game the Rangers deserved it, 4.32 expected goals to 2.85, and our numbers give them the win 64 percent of the time. Some of Seattle's late push is what happens when a team leads by four and sits back; some of it was Berkly Catton, the 20-year-old who set up two goals and has been driving the Kraken's offense lately. Matthew Wood, newly arrived from Nashville in the Shane Wright trade, picked up an assist on Dunn's goal.

New York keeps finding contributions from unexpected places: Kartye, claimed off waivers, keeps scoring, and a fourth line of Chmelar, Noah Laba and Matt Rempe produced a goal. The Rangers will want to know why a 4-0 lead got that close. They will take the two points first.
headline: Rangers build a wall early, then hang on in Seattle
